raw_answer_text:
A1: The first 32-bit word contains the Source Port and Destination Port fields, each 16 bits wide.
A2: The Sequence Number normally indicates the sequence number of the first data octet in that segment; when SYN is set, it instead represents the Initial Sequence Number (ISN), and the first actual data octet is ISN+1.
A3: The Acknowledgment Number is valid only when the ACK control bit is set; when valid, it contains the next sequence number the sender of the segment is expecting to receive.
A4: The Data Offset field specifies the length of the TCP header in 32-bit words; its minimum valid value is 5, corresponding to a minimum header length of 20 bytes.
A5: The same 32-bit word also contains a Reserved field (4 bits, sometimes 6 bits depending on the RFC version), the Control Bits/Flags field (6 or 8 bits), and the Window field (16 bits).
A6: The checksum covers the TCP header, the TCP data, and a pseudo-header consisting of source and destination IP addresses, protocol number, and TCP segment length (fields drawn from the IP header).
A7: The Urgent Pointer's value is meaningful only when the URG control bit is set; when valid, it indicates the offset from the sequence number in the segment to the last octet of urgent data.
A8: The Options field appears only when TCP options are needed (i.e., when Data Offset > 5); the maximum total TCP header length, including options and padding, is 60 bytes.
